High-Level Requirement:
  Summary: List userSessions in admin console is slow
  Description: When you have cluster environment and 100K userSessions, then showing tab "Sessions" is a bit slow.
There is related KEYCLOAK-3298, which fixed the bulk removal of user sessions. For view we need to:
- Doublecheck there is not regression compared to Keycloak 3.1 (ie. all user sessions of logged users are correctly shown in realms, clients and users tabs in admin console). This needs to be done before 3.2 release
- Doublecheck if something can be improved regarding performance of view. Like:
-- pagination of userSessions
-- Count sessions just approximately
Also doublecheck if other usecases, which are using infinispan streams have good performance (showing user sessions of single user or clients, showing offline sessions etc)
Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Cross DC support for User Sessions
  Description: Support user session in cross DC setups. To achieve this we will need to reduce read/writes to user sessions and ideally allow asynchronous replication of user sessions so that we can replicate sessions cross DC.
Considerations:
* Session management both for users and admins
* Logout of clients
* OIDC code to token requests
* OIDC refresh token requests
* OIDC token introspection requests
* Currently keep protocol mappers and scope in session
* SSO idle
* One-time authorization code currently maintained in session
* Refresh token single-use currently maintained in session
* Currently would require synchronous replication as it's a simple is the session there or not

-- login/logout user
-- Showing tab "sessions" from account management
- Some admin events like:

High-Level Requirement:
  Summary: List userSessions in admin console is slow
  Description: When you have cluster environment and 100K userSessions, then showing tab "Sessions" is a bit slow.
There is related KEYCLOAK-3298, which fixed the bulk removal of user sessions. For view we need to:
- Doublecheck there is not regression compared to Keycloak 3.1 (ie. all user sessions of logged users are correctly shown in realms, clients and users tabs in admin console). This needs to be done before 3.2 release
- Doublecheck if something can be improved regarding performance of view. Like:
-- pagination of userSessions
-- Count sessions just approximately
Also doublecheck if other usecases, which are using infinispan streams have good performance (showing user sessions of single user or clients, showing offline sessions etc)
Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Check if ClearExpiredUserSessions can be optimized or removed
  Description: The ClearExpiredUserSessions is background task periodically triggered. When it is in progress, it does lots of possible uneffective operations and unecessary network calls. This can have the impact on performance.
The issues are:
- It iterates over all userSessions and then remove them one-by-one. Same for remoteCache (in case that cross-dc integration is enabled). The ideal is, that the method UserSessionProvider.removeExpired is removed entirely. Which means that when we add/update userSession and clientSession entities, we may need to use the "cache.put" or "cache.replace" operations with the expiration/maxIdle parameters. This would mean that infinispan (JDG for the remoteCache) will take care of removing expired entities. This probably applies to offline sessions and loginFailure entities as well.
- Same can be done for authenticationSessions (That is not so urgent as it is not applicable for JDG and hopefully authenticationSessions will be local, but still will be good to do)
- UserSessionPersister.removeExpired needs to be fixed as well to avoid iterating over all realms. Can be done as part of KEYCLOAK-16802
- All the issues above are especially bad in case there is big number of realms as periodic tasks iterate over all realms. When this JIRA and KEYCLOAK-16802 is fixed, iterating over all realms can be avoided.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Improve performance of JpaUserSessionPersisterProvider.removeExpired
  Description: The JpaUserSessionPersisterProvider.removeExpired is currently called from ClearExpiredUserSessions. It is called separately for each realm and it calls 2 SQL to delete expired entities. Hence for deployment with 5K realms, there are 10K SQL commands called to delete expired sessions.
Moreover ClearExpiredUserSessions needs to iterate over all realms, which is bad performance - will be fixed together with KEYCLOAK-16755

  Description: Currently it's already mechanism to ensure that LastSessionRefreshes are send to the other DC periodically in "batches", so that there is no need to send cross-dc message between DCs for every refreshToken request.
In some cases, there is still the message sent immediately to the other DC (For example when refreshToken request comes in time 29:59 and idle timeout is 30 minutes, it's send immediately because otherwise the other DC will receive update later for example in time 31:04 (assuming 5 seconds for sending the message between DC). It will be a window when it will treat the correct refreshToken as incorrect). We want to always skip that and instead allow some window when refreshTokens will be still allowed (EG. refreshToken will be allowed in idleTimeout+2 minutes. IdleTimeout periodic cleaner thread will use idleTimeout+4 minutes).
The only exception will be the case with "revokeRefreshToken", which will still send requests immediately for now.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Check if ClearExpiredUserSessions can be optimized or removed
  Description: The ClearExpiredUserSessions is background task periodically triggered. When it is in progress, it does lots of possible uneffective operations and unecessary network calls. This can have the impact on performance.
The issues are:
- It iterates over all userSessions and then remove them one-by-one. Same for remoteCache (in case that cross-dc integration is enabled). The ideal is, that the method UserSessionProvider.removeExpired is removed entirely. Which means that when we add/update userSession and clientSession entities, we may need to use the "cache.put" or "cache.replace" operations with the expiration/maxIdle parameters. This would mean that infinispan (JDG for the remoteCache) will take care of removing expired entities. This probably applies to offline sessions and loginFailure entities as well.
- Same can be done for authenticationSessions (That is not so urgent as it is not applicable for JDG and hopefully authenticationSessions will be local, but still will be good to do)
- UserSessionPersister.removeExpired needs to be fixed as well to avoid iterating over all realms. Can be done as part of KEYCLOAK-16802
- All the issues above are especially bad in case there is big number of realms as periodic tasks iterate over all realms. When this JIRA and KEYCLOAK-16802 is fixed, iterating over all realms can be avoided.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Many realms: Background tasks try to cache all realms
  Description: h2. What
When testing with 500-1000 realms, I can see the stacktrace like below (section "Stacktrace") from time to time. The reason is that background tasks (ClearExpiredEvents, ClearExpiredUserSessions) iterate over all realms and try to cache them. The attempt to cache each realm causes lots of SQL calls to the DB as the realm are cached "eagerly" (all the entities are loaded from DB to be allow to fully cache realm). More details in the CachedRealm constructor.
I've tested with Keycloak 9 (RHSSO 7.4). The latest Keycloak master has some changes related to model, however I suppose this issue exists in the master as well (Not 100% sure).
This can maybe affect performance tests triggered for server HTTP requests, which can be slower due the lots of DB calls needed to cache all the realms. But not 100% sure
h2. Workaround
Make sure that standalone.xml is re-configured for example like this:
{code}
<scheduled-task-interval>9000</scheduled-task-interval>
{code}
But this can have other side-effects (lots of dead sessions etc)
h2. Possible solution
Probably short-term (Long term might be new store improvements):
- Background tasks don't try to "cache the world", but just do their jobs
- Caching of the realm itself is improved like:
-- Not cache whole realm in single step. For example re-use DefaultLazyLoader , which is already used for users?
-- Not so much "boilerplate" entities needed for each realm (EG. 5 authentication flows and much more authentication executions even if authentication flows are unchanged)

  Summary: Valid Redirect URI for review apps (wildcard in hostname?)
  Description: I'm using gitlab to handle code and it has this great feature called "review apps". This feature makes every feature branch deployed to a site so interested parties can review it before it is merged. So if you create a new branch called "my-cool-feature" it will automatically deploy to a site called "my-cool-feature.myapp.mycompany.com".
Now I wanted to use review apps with an application that is protected by keycloak. Everything worked great until I got to the Valid Redirect URI part. I previously did not understand that it only accepted a wildcard at the end. The origin URI accepts wildcards in the hostname so I found it natural that redirect uri would too. However after reading the documentation I found this section:
> Wildcards ( * ) are only allowed at the end of a URI, i.e. 
So my question is if there is any possibility to add a feature that allows for use with this kind of dynamic sites. I cannot really predict all the feature branch names that developers will create so they cannot really be pre-registered. If valid redirect URI would allow for something like that would solve it directly. I found some previous discussions about having a wildcard in the host part:
Of course there are the usual security concerns etc. I think having a wildcard in the host of valid redirect uri would be really useful for some development scenarios but should probably not be used in production. It would be nice if I as a server admin could make that decision though, instead of not having the option at all. Also I think with the cloud, container, and k8s environments we have today everything is more dynamic, sites are created and deleted on a daily basis with potentially dynamic hostnames. So having this function today is probably more motivated than back in 2016.
However, my scenario is just using keycloak to secure these review apps that appear on dynamic sites. If there is a different way to achieve it other than allowing wildcards in the hostname I could use that instead :-).

  Description: In our performance tests, we currently use a "closed" workload injection model* which is characterized by a constant number of active users. - more realistic workload

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Many realms: Background tasks try to cache all realms
  Description: h2. What
When testing with 500-1000 realms, I can see the stacktrace like below (section "Stacktrace") from time to time. The reason is that background tasks (ClearExpiredEvents, ClearExpiredUserSessions) iterate over all realms and try to cache them. The attempt to cache each realm causes lots of SQL calls to the DB as the realm are cached "eagerly" (all the entities are loaded from DB to be allow to fully cache realm). More details in the CachedRealm constructor.
I've tested with Keycloak 9 (RHSSO 7.4). The latest Keycloak master has some changes related to model, however I suppose this issue exists in the master as well (Not 100% sure).
This can maybe affect performance tests triggered for server HTTP requests, which can be slower due the lots of DB calls needed to cache all the realms. But not 100% sure
h2. Workaround
Make sure that standalone.xml is re-configured for example like this:
{code}
<scheduled-task-interval>9000</scheduled-task-interval>
{code}
But this can have other side-effects (lots of dead sessions etc)
h2. Possible solution
Probably short-term (Long term might be new store improvements):
- Background tasks don't try to "cache the world", but just do their jobs
- Caching of the realm itself is improved like:
-- Not cache whole realm in single step. For example re-use DefaultLazyLoader , which is already used for users?
-- Not so much "boilerplate" entities needed for each realm (EG. 5 authentication flows and much more authentication executions even if authentication flows are unchanged)

  Description: Epic brief: 
Summary: Add support to use FIDO2 and FIDO U2F security keys for two factor authentication
Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Support for attestation statement verification
  Description: First version of W3C Web Authentication support ( KEYCLOAK-9360 ) doesn't have support for attestation statement verification.
This JIRA will require:
- Adding options "Indirect" and "Direct" to Attestation Conveyance Preference in the WebAuthn policy.
- Ensure that proper webauthn4j functions are called based on the requested attestation conveyance preference
- Introducing of apache-kerby-asn1 library as a Wildfly module may be needed for verify android and TPM attestation statements (which will require that RH is able to productize it, so may require some other subtask related to that).
- Ability to obtain trust anchors.
[~tnorimat] mentioned in the design document 
{code}
In order to verify Attestation Statement, keycloak needs to get its trust anchor's certificate. It is plausible to get the trust anchor's certificate in the following ways :
- obtained from FIDO Alliance Metadata Services.
- obtained from an authenticator's vendor.
{code}
Not sure it makes sense, but we can check if we can use the existing TrustStore SPI available in Keycloak. The SPI allows to have set of known trusted certificates. For performance (or other) purpose, it can be beneficial if the certificate of authenticator's vendor is added manually to the truststore file used by Keycloak and hence will be always available without a need to somehow obtain it from the authenticator. That's to be investigated whether this is valid option or not...
When this feature is to be supported, it is needed to consider the above two ways to get the trust anchors' certificates.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: WebAuthn: polish after rebase
  Description: After rebase prototype with latest Keycloak master, WebAuthn was added to the prototype as it is already available in latest Keycloak master. We may have some remaining things to discuss & clarify. This JIRA is just to handle this possible remaining work around clarifying those points.
In case we agree that there is nothing more needed, we may just close the JIRA :)
The points were discussed on zulip (room #dev-auth and topic "multi-factor rebase"), so just copy/paste it here:
1) I've added the WebAuthnCredentialModel class (compatible with OTPCredentialModel and PasswordCredentialModel introduced in the prototype) and I've added fields 
"aaguid", "credentialId" and "counter" as part of CredentialData and "attestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" as part of SecretData. The only reason why I did is, 
that secretData are not displayed in the admin console. See screenshot Screenshot-from-2019-10-23-11-39-46.png
I am not sure if displaying "AttestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" won't make the data too big. But strictly said, WebAuthn credential doesn't have any confidential data. So should be "attestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" added to CredentialData too and displayed in the admin console? This will mean secretData will be just empty. WDYT?
2) The WebAuthn works in a bit different way than OTP. The WebAuthn authentication javascript call to "navigator.credentials.get" allows to pass more IDs of webAuthn credentials to the list of "allowed-credentials" and client itself can decide which credential he wants to use. So regarding this, I see few options:
a) The WebAuthnAuthenticator won't inherit from CredentialValidator interface. This means that in the Credentials selector list, which is described here there will be just single label "WebAuthn" . When this label is chosen, the checkbox is displayed when user can select the WebAuthn credentials, which he wants to use. This is the approach, which I used so far and you can see the screenshot how it looks like the screenshot Screenshot-from-2019-10-23-11-15-49.png
b) The WebAuthnAuthenticator will inherit from CredentialValidator interface. So Credentials selector list will contain separate items for each credential with labels like "WebAuthn - yubikey", "WebAuthn - chrome test" . There won't be checkbox selection on the page. So WebAuthn call to "navigator.credentials.get" will be always called just with single allowed credential.
c) Hybrid of 2 options above. There will be 2 labels and when particular label is chosen, the checkbox selection will be displayed as well on the WebAuthn page, but just with the single credential selected by default, which will correspond to the selected label. User has ability to select more credentials if he wants.
3) I removed the attributes from UserModel as I mentioned. Regarding the credentialId, I kept it just as single item in the WebAuthnCredentialData. In the keycloak master, you had it saved defacto 2 times:
a) the user attribute, which corresponds to the Base64URL encoded "rawId" returned from navigator.credentials.create
b) The attribute on the credential, which corresponds to the Base64 encoded of AttestedCredentialData.getCredentialId .
It seems to me from the WebAuthn specification and from my testing with yubikey and chrome testing api, that both those "credentialsId" are defacto same. So is it ok to save it just once in the credential model? In other words, the item returned from "rawId" is not saved.

  Summary: Allow user to choose from multiple credential types during registration of 2-factor credential during authentication
  Description: Let's assume we have authentication flow configured like this:
{code}
Auth type   | Requirement
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cookie   [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled 
Kerberos   [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
Identity Provider Redirector [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled 
Authenticate with Keycloak [x] Alternative [ ] Required [ ] Conditional [ ] Disabled 
 | - Username Password Form [ ] Alternative [x] Required  [ ] Disabled
 | - Authenticate with MFA [ ] Alternative [x] Required [ ] Conditional [ ] Disabled 
 | - OTP   [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
 | - WebAuthn  [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
 | - Hardware Token [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
{code}
Then let's assume that user doesn't yet have any 2-factor credential (OTP or WebAuthn or Hardware Token) configured on his account. So then he should be required to configure either OTP or WebAuthn credential during authentication. In this case, after he finish password authentication, he should be able to choose if he wants to configure OTP or WebAuthn credential and register one of them. He should be able to go back and select different credential (EG. He first clicks on WebAuthn, but then he change his mind because he doesn't have yubikey and his phone doesn't have bluetooth, so he want to go back and register OTP through the Google Authenticator app on his phone)

This signature is then sent to the IDP and thus allows access to the user in the original triggering channel. The only thing the user has to supply original triggering channel is a user identifier, no credentials.
There are two two related standards for this
* (Old & depericated) OIDC Modrna CIBA @
* (New) OIDC Modrna FAPI CIBA @
** This also has the Logding Intent mechanism to allow transaction data (that is to be signed by the user mobile device) to be sent via the back channel and the returned scope_id can then be sent via the standard OIDC mechanims.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Unable to add more than 6 acceptable AAGUIDs for WebAuthn
  Description: h2. Summary
Only 6 AAGUIDs can be added to the Acceptable AAGUID field under WebAuthn Policy of the Keycloak Admin Console because the underlying database column only allows 255 characters. We should be able to whitelist more than 6 AAGUIDs. 
h2. Details
An authenticator device used by WebAuthn contains an AAUID that can be used to identify the type of the authenticator. Each AAGUID is 36 characters long including hyphens (ex. 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000). 
These AAGUID can be whitelisted in Keycloak Admin Console via Authentication -> WebAuthn Policy -> Acceptable AAGUIDs. This list of AAGUIDs is then converted into one comma separated string by org.keycloak.models.jpa.RealmAdapter.setWebAuthnPolicy() then inserted into the "value" column of "realm_attribute" table in Keycloak's database. 
However, because this column is only 255 characters long, only six AAGUID can be added (6 x 36 AAGUID characters + 5 commas = 221 total characters). Adding more than 6 will fail with an error message. 
There should be support for whitelisting more than 6 AAGUIDs.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: WebAuthn: create authenticator, requiredAction and policy for passwordless
  Description: h3. What
Regarding WebAuthn, we need to ensure that user is able to register WebAuthn Security Key as passwordless authenticator (1st factor) or as 2nd factor authenticator. 
In other words, WebAuthn is example of the credential, which is probably useful as both 1st factor or 2nd factor. There may be different requirement for WebAuthn configuration for those 2 cases. For example for passwordless WebAuthn, it may be needed that "userRequired" is set to "required" in WebAuthn policy and for 2nd factor WebAuthn, it may be needed that "userRequired" is set to "preferred" .
h3. 
h3. How
Proper solution will be the possibility to create "instances" of credential policy rather than rely on java providers. But until that is done, we will go with a workaround, which may be like this:
- Adding another subclass of WebAuthnAuthenticator. Something like "WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator
- Adding another subclass of WebAuthnRegister. Something like "WebAuthnPasswordlessRegister" . The WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator will be tight to this required action
- Adding another subclass of WebAuthnCredentialProvider like "WebAuthnPasswordlessCredentialProvider" . It will be used by WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator and WebAuthnPasswordlessRegister.
- Adding another tab in admin console. In addition to the current tab "WebAuthn policy", we will add another tab like "WebAuthn PasswordLess Policy" . The existing tab "WebAuthn Policy" may be renamed to something like "WebAuthn 2nd-factor policy" . The admin will be able to configure different policies for passwordless and different for 2nd factor.
- The previous point means that we may need to add some new set of fields to RealmRepresentation object. All the "webAuthn*" properties may have another counterpart for passwordless. For example "webAuthnPolicyRpEntityName" will have "webAuthnPasswordlessPolicyRpEntityName" .
- The WebAuthnPasswordLessAuthenticator, WebAuthnPasswordLessRegister and WebAuthnPasswordlessCredentialProvider will read the configuration from the "passwordless" fields, but otherwise their implementation will be same as for the 2nd factor java classes.
Those points will allow administrator to configure separate policies for 1st-factor and 2nd-factor and add separate authenticators to authentication flow for 1st-factor and 2-nd factor. Also it will allow user to have 2 type of webauthn credentials. Credentials of type "webauthn-passwordless" for 1st factor WebAuthn authentication and "webauthn" for 2nd factor WebAuthn authentication (NOTE: The credential type "webauthn" is already used in latest master, so we will keep it for backwards-compatibility and won't rename it)
This whole thing is a workaround, which will be addressed more properly in the future.
